Issued at 225 PM EDT Wed Aug 26 2026

Today-Tonight... Upper level high pressure across the Atlantic and 
across the TX/SW US will remain in place today, with Florida 
residing between the two high pressures. Shortwave energy will 
traverse near and over Florida through the day. At the surface, high 
pressure across the Atlantic will slowly shift northward, with the 
axis remaining over the Florida peninsula. Locally, south to 
southwest flow will persist, with the east coast sea breeze forecast 
to form in the afternoon and push inland, turning the winds onshore. 
Moisture over the local area will be near to slightly above normal 
for this time of year, with PW values ranging from 1.7-2.1". this 
coupled with energy aloft will support convection this afternoon.
Scattered showers and storms have already formed around the I-95
corridor this afternoon along the east coast sea breeze. Additional
showers and lightning storms are forecast to form across the 
interior along boundary collisions between sea breezes and outflow
boundaries by late afternoon and into the early evening. Coverage
of showers and lightning storms today will be medium to high, 
with 50-60 percent chance of rain along the coast, and 60-70 
percent chance of rain across the interior. 

The environment supports storms with  plenty of instability (MUCAPE 
1800-2500 J/kg), ample buoyancy (lifted index of -4 to -7), 
sufficient downdraft potential (DCAPE 800-1050 J/kg).  Main storm 
hazards will be frequent lightning, gusty winds of 45-55 mph, and 
heavy rainfall of 1-3 " which may lead to minor localized flooding 
in urban and poor drainage areas. Any lingering activity will 
diminish around midnight, with activity across the Atlantic waters 
continuing through the overnight. Temperatures will be near to 
slightly above normal, with afternoon highs in the low to mid 90s 
with peak heat indices of 100-105F. Overnight lows will be in the 
low to mid 70s. 

The National Hurricane Center (NHC) continues to give a tropical 
wave in the Atlantic a 60% chance of tropical cyclone formation over 
the next couple of days. While it is far too early to know whether 
this feature will affect the U.S., it's a reminder to be prepared as 
we head into peak hurricane season.

Thursday-Friday... Florida will remain situated between two upper 
level high pressure systems, one in the Atlantic and one over TX/SW 
US, as an upper level trough shift eastward towards the eastern US. 
Shortwave energy will continue to traverse the base of this trough 
over the Deep South and across the Florida peninsula. At the 
surface, high pressure across the Atlantic will slowly shift 
northward, with the axis remaining over Florida. Locally, offshore (S-
SW) flow will persist with speeds 5-10 mph each day. The east coast 
sea breeze is forecast to form each afternoon, turning the winds 
onshore (E-SE) as the sea breeze pushes inland. Moisture will remain 
near to slightly above normal, with PW values 1.8-2.3" each day. 
This will support a medium to high (50-70 percent) chance of showers 
and storms through the period. Highest coverage will be across the 
interior each afternoon and evening where the sea breeze and outflow 
boundary collisions are forecast to occur. Main storm hazards will 
be frequent lightning, gusty winds of 45-55mph, and locally heavy 
rainfall. Temperatures will be seasonably hot and humid into late 
week, with overnight lows remaining warm and muggy.  

Saturday-Wednesday... Upper level high pressure over the Atlantic 
and the SW US will merge over the weekend and remain over the 
southern US/Gulf/Atlantic into early next week. At the surface, high 
pressure over the Atlantic will continue to shift northward towards 
the Carolinas into early next week. A frontal boundary will slide 
southward into the Deep South/Northern Florida this weekend before 
stalling, eventually becoming diffuse by early next week. Locally, 
winds will shift onshore (east to southeast) this weekend and remain 
through at least mid next week as the surface high pressure moves 
northward of Florida. Moisture across the local area will remain 
near to above normal, with PW values of 1.8-2.1". Daily afternoon 
showers and lightning storms are forecast to continue, with 
scattered storms forming each day along the advancing east coast sea 
breeze, with additional showers and storms forming across the 
interior. Highest coverage of storms will be across the interior, 
where the sea breeze collision is forecast to occur each evening. 
Storm hazards will be similar to what they are today through late 
week. Temperatures will remain seasonably hot and humid with 
overnight lows warm and muggy.
